packages.title: Load platform trust roots by default
deliverables: Add Trust to src/transport/trust.zig. It is union(enum) { platform, pem: []const u8 }. Trust.platformPem(allocator, io, now) calls std.crypto.Certificate.Bundle.rescan, then writes each DER root in bundle.map as a PEM block. Appendix A has the measured loop. rescan reads the Linux bundle paths, the macOS SystemRootCertificates.keychain, and the Windows ROOT store, so one code path covers the three release targets.

Replace transport.Options.ca_pem: ?[]const u8 with trust: Trust = .platform. Client.init resolves .platform to PEM bytes once per client. Raise max_ca_bytes to 2 MiB. Delete the error.Unavailable return at src/transport/root.zig:120. An empty platform bundle fails Client.init with error.Unavailable and the frontend prints no trusted certificate roots found. Set FOO_CA_FILE or SSL_CERT_FILE to a PEM bundle.

In App.httpClient, choose the trust source in this order. FOO_CA_FILE as Trust.pem, then SSL_CERT_FILE as Trust.pem, then Trust.platform. Keep loadRoots for both file paths. SSL_CERT_FILE is the variable Codex, Bun, and OpenSSL honor, so a Nix shell or a corporate image works with no foo-specific setting.
Leave nix/transport.nix and .github/scripts/build-transport.py unchanged. Trust comes from the Zig standard library, not from a curl build flag. Appendix B records why.

Add platform_trust to tests/transport/probe.zig Mode. It opens a client with .trust = .platform and fetches the URL. In tests/transport/fixtures.py, add test_platform_trust_rejects_fixture_ca, which runs platform_trust against the loopback TLS server and expects IoFailure with .unsent because the fixture CA is not a platform root, and test_ssl_cert_file_override, which sets SSL_CERT_FILE to tests/transport/tls/ca.pem and expects 200.
acceptance: nix develop -c zig build run -- run --prompt hi --config /tmp/opencode/ca-proto/probe.json with no FOO_CA_FILE reaches api.openai.com and fails on the missing key, not on TLS. Before U02 the line reads foo: run ended with provider_error. After U02 it names the 401.
tests/integration/check.py no longer mentions FOO_CA_FILE.
Tests alone are not sufficient verification. The unit, live, and perf boxes in docs/plan/usability.md are all checked.
handoff: Checked plan section in docs/plan/usability.md with evidence per box.
Swarm verdict at the exact head SHA, base and head SHAs recorded.

Stop keeps its seven variants. A provider_error outcome always carries a detail.

Add Exchange.status: ?u16 and Exchange.retry_after_ms: ?u64 in src/providers/root.zig and fill them in head() so the status and retry-after header travel with error.Authentication, error.RateLimited, and error.Rejected. packages.title: Define a provider once and list its models under it
deliverables: Add Provider to src/contracts/config.zig. Fields are family: Family, base_url: []const u8, credential: SecretRef, headers: []const Header, options_json, and models: []const ModelEntry. ModelEntry has id, name: ?[]const u8, options_json, max_output_tokens, and endpoint: ?[]const u8. The resolver appends the family route to base_url, /responses, /chat/completions, or /messages. A ModelEntry.endpoint replaces the join for one model, which covers gateways with per-model paths. This is the Pi shape, with models nested under the provider, and the OpenCode shape for the same reason.

Keep Resolved.model: Model. finish() computes it by joining the selected entry with its provider. The adapter sends literal keys and fails authentication for unresolved auth references. The flattened model preserves journal identity.

Add root keys providers and model. providers is an object keyed by provider id. Each value has the Provider fields and models as an object keyed by model id. model is a string provider/id. Delete the root model object. Keep --model, --endpoint, and --credential-env as patches on the selected model and provider.

Merge rules. providers.<id> merges per field across layers, and providers.<id>.models.<id> merges per field. A later layer can add a provider or a model or change a field. null removes a provider or a model. Provenance records providers.<id>.<field> and providers.<id>.models.<id>.<field>. Changing a provider's base_url origin clears its inherited credential and headers, which keeps the rule at src/config/parse.zig:291.

Credential kinds in secret(). Accept {"environment": "VAR"}, {"literal": "..."} for gateways with fixed virtual keys, and {"auth": "<provider-id>"}, which U05 resolves from the token store and which U03 parses and carries. Redact literal in effectiveJson.

Rename --provider FAMILY to --family FAMILY. --model takes provider/id. --endpoint sets the selected model's endpoint. --credential-env sets the selected provider's credential. Add --provider ID as a shorthand that selects the first model of that provider when --model names no provider.
foo config show prints providers with nested models and the resolved model with its provenance.

Rewrite src/config/examples/minimal.json as one provider and one model. Rewrite customized.json with two providers and three models. Rewrite each row of src/providers/routes.md as a providers.<id> snippet.
acceptance: A user config of twelve lines selects a model.

foo config show --model openai/gpt-5.5-mini prints model.id = gpt-5.5-mini with provenance command_line, and max_output_tokens = 2048 with provenance providers.openai.models.gpt-5.5-mini.max_output_tokens.
A config with the old root model object fails foo config check with path model, reason invalid_value, and the message model is a string "provider/id"; define providers under "providers".

packages.title: Add foo auth and a private token store
deliverables: Add CredentialSource to src/auth/root.zig. It is a vtable { context, resolve_fn: fn(ctx, allocator, io.Context, SecretRef) Error!Credential }. Credential is union(enum) { api_key: []const u8, bearer: struct { token: []const u8, account: ?[]const u8 } }. The environment resolver and the store resolver both implement it. Replace the four inline environment lookups at src/providers/root.zig:72, src/cli/root.zig:316, src/contracts/runtime/session.zig:549, and src/mcp/connection_config.zig:32 with calls through one CredentialSource.

Add Store to src/auth/store.zig. The file is <user config dir>/auth.json, where the directory is the one userConfig() in src/cli/arguments.zig:178 resolves. Create it with mode 0o600 through the exclusive-create and symlink-refusing open from src/session/local.zig:187 and :211. Entries are keyed by provider id and hold { "type": "api_key", "key" } or { "type": "oauth", "access", "refresh", "expires_ms", "account" }. Write to a temp file then rename, under a auth.lock taken with the same exclusive lock as src/session/local.zig:31. Reads reject a file with group or world bits set and print chmod 600 <path>.
Add SecretRef.auth: []const u8. The store resolver returns api_key or bearer by entry type and returns error.Authentication for a missing entry.

Add foo auth login <provider-id> [--api-key], foo auth list, and foo auth logout <provider-id>. --api-key reads the key from the terminal without echo and stores it. Without --api-key, login runs the OAuth flow registered for that provider in src/auth/root.zig. U05 ships the registry empty, so login without --api-key prints no browser login for <id>; use --api-key. list prints <id>  <type>  <expires in Nh | no expiry> and never a value.

Add Adapter.credentials: CredentialSource. Call it inside the attempt loop at src/providers/root.zig:30 so a refreshed token is used on a retry. On a 401 with a bearer credential whose entry has a refresh token, refresh once through the registry and retry once. A second 401 surfaces Authentication. This is the one retry that Delivery.possibly_sent permits, because the request was rejected before the model ran.
missingCredential asks the CredentialSource whether the reference resolves. The U02 line ends Set <VAR> for environment and Run foo auth login <id> for auth.
acceptance: foo auth login litellm --api-key prompts litellm API key:, stores it, and foo auth list prints litellm  api_key  no expiry.
stat -c %a ~/.config/foo/auth.json prints 600.
A provider with "credential": {"auth": "litellm"} completes a run with no environment variable set.

packages.title: Log in with a SuperGrok subscription and add OpenCode Go
deliverables: Add the xai device-code flow to the registry with the values in Appendix E. Client id b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828, device endpoint https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/device/code, token endpoint https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token, scope openid profile email offline_access grok-cli:access api:access, grant urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, and referrer=foo. Pi and OpenCode label this "Sign in with SuperGrok or X Premium". Store the result as an oauth entry.

Add built-in providers in src/config/defaults.zig. xai with family openai_responses, base_url https://api.x.ai/v1, credential {"auth": "xai"}. opencode with family openai_responses, base_url https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1, credential {"auth": "opencode"}. opencode-go with the same family, base_url https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1, and credential {"auth": "opencode-go"}. openai with https://api.openai.com/v1 and {"environment": "OPENAI_API_KEY"}. anthropic with family anthropic_messages, https://api.anthropic.com/v1, and {"environment": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"}. A user layer can override any field or set a provider to null.

OpenCode Go and Console sell API keys. There is no OAuth flow. foo auth login opencode --api-key and foo auth login opencode-go --api-key store the key.
